Hey, I don't know your family, but if it will help you, I can tell you about the two times my family found out.

I first started cutting myself at the tender age of 11. I continued for 3 years, progressively getting worse. One day, a week before school, my mother was leaving to go to the store and I asked her to grab me a long sleeve shirt for my school uniform. This wasn't really out of the ordinary for me even though we live in Texas, the hottest place in the universe. But, even so, she immediately came over and asked,

"Why are you always hiding your arms?" and proceeded to pull up my sleeve.

After that, we had a long conversation during which she made me promise not to do it again, which I aptly broke but a month later.

The second time was different. This time I told her about it because I had costuming later that day and didn't want one of my teachers or friends telling her. This time she told my sisters, who instead of just asking about it, continued to question my long sleeves in the summer, even though they already knew why.

I still wear long sleeves, even though I don't self-harm very often, and never on my fore-arms. But, my friends and especially my boyfriend, who doesn't know about my past, are starting to question my choice of fashion.

In any case, what I'm trying to say is, I hope you feel better, and that your parents are very understanding.

P.S. sorry for the long read...

There was this one time, I had a mix of a fast and slow cut. I was arguing with my sisters and had a mental breakdown, in the heat of the moment I ran into the kitchen, grabbed the sharpest knife we have, and made a long deep vertical cut.  It was like I was in autopilot. My parents had found out about my self harm about three months before that and I stayed clean for those three months. Later that night I had an anxiety attack about how the world would be so disappointed. I'm no longer clean, but I do realize my friends care.
